extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors, journalism students, and news organizations
extracted.subtask_description: The Society of Professional Journalists Code of Ethics: a set of guiding principles and specific practice-oriented criteria for ethical journalism across media. It outlines a preamble, four core principles, and detailed behavioral guidance for reporters and news organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preamble: purpose of the code
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of the Society of Professional Journalists believe that public enlightenment is the forerunner of justice and the foundation of democracy. Ethical journalism strives to ensure the free exchange of information that is accurate, fair and thorough. An ethical journalist acts with integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Code is a statement of abiding principles supported by explanations and position papers; it is not a set of rules but a guide encouraging responsibility for information provided, regardless of medium. The code should be read as a whole; individual principles should not be taken out of context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle: Seek Truth and Report It
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethical journalism should be accurate and fair. Journalists should be honest and courageous in gathering, reporting and interpreting information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This principle frames many specific practices (see detailed bullets) emphasizing verification, context, transparency about sources, and avoiding distortion or plagiarism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek Truth — Take responsibility for accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Take responsibility for the accuracy of their work. Verify information before releasing it. Use original sources whenever possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists must verify facts and prefer original-source material rather than relying on summaries or secondhand reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek Truth — Speed and format do not excuse inaccuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Remember that neither speed nor format excuses inaccuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even under deadline pressure or in new formats (social media, live updates), accuracy must not be sacrificed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek Truth — Provide context and avoid misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide context. Take special care not to misrepresent or oversimplify in promoting, previewing or summarizing a story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Headlines, teasers, and summaries should not distort the substance of reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek Truth — Update and correct throughout a story's life
rubrics_metrics.description: Gather, update and correct information throughout the life of a news story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting is ongoing; new facts should be incorporated and corrections made as information evolves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek Truth — Keep and honor promises
rubrics_metrics.description: Be cautious when making promises, but keep the promises they make.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully consider commitments (e.g., off-the-record agreements) and fulfill them unless ethically compelled otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek Truth — Identify sources clearly
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify sources clearly. The public is entitled to as much information as possible to judge the reliability and motivations of sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide readers/viewers with sufficient sourcing information to assess credibility, unless anonymity is justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek Truth — Consider motives before granting anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider sources' motives before promising anonymity. Reserve anonymity for sources who may face danger, retribution or other harm, and have information that cannot be obtained elsewhere. Explain why anonymity was granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anonymity should be exceptional, justified, and explained to audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek Truth — Give subjects opportunity to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: Diligently seek subjects of news coverage to allow them to respond to criticism or allegations of wrongdoing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters should attempt to contact subjects prior to publication when allegations or criticisms are involved, and include their responses where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek Truth — Avoid undercover/surreptitious methods unless necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid undercover or other surreptitious methods of gathering information unless traditional, open methods will not yield information vital to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secret methods require strong public-interest justification and should be a last resort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek Truth — Hold power accountable; give voice to the voiceless
rubrics_metrics.description: Be vigilant and courageous about holding those with power accountable. Give voice to the voiceless.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists have a watchdog role and should seek out underrepresented perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek Truth — Support open exchange of views
rubrics_metrics.description: Support the open and civil exchange of views, even views they find repugnant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage should include a range of viewpoints and enable civil discourse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek Truth — Serve as watchdog over public affairs and records
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize a special obligation to serve as watchdogs over public affairs and government. Seek to ensure that the public's business is conducted in the open, and that public records are open to all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists should pursue transparency and access to public information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek Truth — Provide access to source material when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide access to source material when it is relevant and appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When possible, share documents, data, and materials that substantiate reporting, balancing privacy and legal constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek Truth — Tell diverse human stories and seek unheard voices
rubrics_metrics.description: Boldly tell the story of the diversity and magnitude of the human experience. Seek sources whose voices we seldom hear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively avoid narrow sourcing; include perspectives across communities and experiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek Truth — Avoid stereotyping and check biases
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid stereotyping. Journalists should examine the ways their values and experiences may shape their reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflect on and mitigate personal and cultural biases in reporting and sourcing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek Truth — Label advocacy and commentary
rubrics_metrics.description: Label advocacy and commentary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly distinguish opinion, analysis, and advocacy from straight news reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek Truth — Never deliberately distort facts or context
rubrics_metrics.description: Never deliberately distort facts or context, including visual information. Clearly label illustrations and re-enactments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photos, videos, and other visuals must not be manipulated in ways that mislead; staged elements should be identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek Truth — Never plagiarize; always attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: Never plagiarize. Always attribute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect intellectual property and give clear credit for others' work and ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle: Minimize Harm
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethical journalism treats sources, subjects, colleagues and members of the public as human beings deserving of respect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This principle directs journalists to weigh harm, show compassion, and consider privacy and consequences before publishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize Harm — Balance public need vs potential harm
rubrics_metrics.description: Balance the public's need for information against potential harm or discomfort. Pursuit of the news is not a license for arrogance or undue intrusiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether publication serves significant public interest relative to potential damage to individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize Harm — Show compassion and sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Show compassion for those who may be affected by news coverage. Use heightened sensitivity when dealing with juveniles, victims of sex crimes, and sources or subjects who are inexperienced or unable to give consent. Consider cultural differences in approach and treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise extra care with vulnerable people and consider trauma-informed reporting practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize Harm — Legal access is not always ethical justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that legal access to information differs from an ethical justification to publish or broadcast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Just because information is obtainable legally does not mean it should be published without weighing ethical consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize Harm — Respect greater privacy rights of private people
rubrics_metrics.description: Realize that private people have a greater right to control information about themselves than public figures and others who seek power, influence or attention. Weigh the consequences of publishing or broadcasting personal information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate between public figures and private individuals when deciding what personal information is necessary to publish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize Harm — Avoid pandering to lurid curiosity
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid pandering to lurid curiosity, even if others do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resist sensationalism that serves prurient interest rather than public understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize Harm — Balance suspects' fair trial rights with public's right to know
rubrics_metrics.description: Balance a suspect's right to a fair trial with the public's right to know. Consider the implications of identifying criminal suspects before they face legal charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious about naming or heavily profiling suspects before formal charges to avoid prejudicing legal processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize Harm — Consider long-term implications and permanence
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider the long-term implications of the extended reach and permanence of publication. Provide updated and more complete information as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remember that online content persists; correct, update, and contextualize past coverage when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle: Act Independently
rubrics_metrics.description: The highest and primary obligation of ethical journalism is to serve the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists should avoid influences that compromise independence and disclose unavoidable conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act Independently — Avoid conflicts of interest; disclose unavoidable ones
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid conflicts of interest, real or perceived. Disclose unavoidable conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain independence from subjects of reporting; be transparent when conflicts exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act Independently — Refuse gifts and avoid compromising activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Refuse gifts, favors, fees, free travel and special treatment, and avoid political and other outside activities that may compromise integrity or impartiality, or may damage credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steer clear of benefits that could create obligation or influence coverage; maintain clear separation between reporting and external engagements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act Independently — Do not pay for access; identify outside-provided content
rubrics_metrics.description: Be wary of sources offering information for favors or money; do not pay for access to news. Identify content provided by outside sources, whether paid or not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid buying information that could bias reporting; disclose sponsored or externally supplied content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act Independently — Deny favored treatment to advertisers/donors/special interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Deny favored treatment to advertisers, donors or any other special interests, and resist internal and external pressure to influence coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain editorial independence from commercial and financial pressures; ensure coverage decisions are not swayed by funders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act Independently — Distinguish news from advertising; label sponsored content
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish news from advertising and shun hybrids that blur the lines between the two. Prominently label sponsored content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make clear to audiences when material is advertising or advertorial to preserve trust and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle: Be Accountable and Transparent
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethical journalism means taking responsibility for one's work and explaining one's decisions to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accountability includes promptly addressing errors, explaining choices, and encouraging dialogue with the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Accountable — Explain ethical choices and processes to audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain ethical choices and processes to audiences. Encourage a civil dialogue with the public about journalistic practices, coverage and news content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be open about methods, sourcing decisions, and ethical trade-offs to foster public trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Accountable — Respond quickly to questions about accuracy, clarity, fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Respond quickly to questions about accuracy, clarity and fairness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain accessible channels for audience feedback and address concerns in a timely manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Accountable — Acknowledge mistakes and correct promptly and prominently
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge mistakes and correct them promptly and prominently. Explain corrections and clarifications carefully and clearly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections should be visible and accompanied by explanations of what was wrong and why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Accountable — Expose unethical conduct in journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Expose unethical conduct in journalism, including within their organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate and report misconduct in the profession and within one's own organization when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Accountable — Abide by the same high standards expected of others
rubrics_metrics.description: Abide by the same high standards they expect of others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists and news organizations should model the ethical behavior they demand from sources and peers.
